threads.body: [General] This predicate only establishes that the relative reduction is smaller, but the selected message also claims that the absolute saving is larger. For example, no-agent 4→2 and agent 10→9 would report that 1 second is larger than 2 seconds. Include the absolute comparison in this branch (or split the wording) so the generated interpretation remains factual.

replies.body:
Addressed in 82ee419eef73d911108ee55f3c61fd0fcb60a12a.

Analysis: The predicate checked that both savings were positive and that the relative reduction was smaller with the agent. It did not check the absolute comparison described by the selected message. Requiring the agent saving to exceed the no-agent saving keeps that wording factual, while the fallback reports both measured values for other combinations.

Upsides: The report no longer makes a false absolute comparison. The regression test covers the reviewer's 4-to-2 and 10-to-9 example.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: [Performance] StartupTimings.parse() collects all log lines into a List via logs.lines().toList() before iterating. For large container logs (especially in preflight with extra logging enabled), this adds avoidable allocation and copy; you can iterate the stream directly without materializing a list.

replies.body:
Addressed in be763488d70cee99b51da2587cb248892ec29fc0.

Analysis: StartupTimings.parse() only needs one pass over the log text. An Iterator from String.lines() preserves the existing validation and duplicate detection while avoiding the intermediate List.

Upsides: Avoids allocating and copying every log line before parsing.

Downsides: Uses an explicit iterator loop instead of an enhanced for loop.
